observations: Photo 0 and 1 show the same automotive ECU module with exposed multi-colored wiring harness, lying on bare dirt/sand ground.
Photo 1 close-up shows a legible label: VW logo, part number 07K 906 055 CR, 07K 907 309 A, 'Benzin ME17.5.6', 'Assembled in Mexico', Bosch logo, 'Bosch 0261 S07 862', 'Motronic', date code 13-03-09.
Photo 0 shows the underside/wiring side of the same unit with a plate reading 'Spain KJV 6Q0 907 590 C 51.72'.
Photo 2 shows a different, separate ECU module, metal casing, also on dirt, with a cut/taped wiring loom and no clearly readable part number (only partial faint text, 'Germany' visible).
All units show dirt, wear, scratches consistent with used/salvage parts; wiring looks cut away from a harness rather than from a connector, suggesting removal from a scrapped vehicle.
Watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' overlaid on all photos (seller's branding, not proof of Porsche stock).
No testing equipment, bench test, or diagnostic screen shown in any photo.

claims.claim: We also deal in car spare parts for Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche and Bentley
claims.evidence: Only a VW-branded ECU is shown in photos; no Audi, Porsche, or Bentley parts are pictured.

claims.claim: Implied working condition of the ECU (not stated but typical for resale)
claims.evidence: No bench test, dashboard light, or diagnostic readout shown; wires appear cut, not connector-terminated.

risks.risk: ECU may be electronically immobilizer-locked to the donor vehicle, requiring costly coding/matching to work in a buyer's car
risks.proof: Seller statement or photo of an unlock/EEPROM reset certificate, or confirmation it is sold as 'virgin'/unlocked
risks.if_unproven: priced as locked/non-plug-and-play, i.e. lowest functional value

risks.risk: Unit may be non-functional (dead, corroded pins, water damage) since it was pulled with cut wires and left on bare dirt
risks.proof: Video of ECU powering up on a test bench or clear continuity/boot-up test

risks.risk: Second ECU in photo 2 is a different, unidentified part number — may not even be VW/Audi/Porsche/Bentley compatible as claimed
risks.proof: Close-up photo of its label/part number plate
risks.if_unproven: treated as unidentified part, not priced alongside the named VW unit

risks.risk: Physical damage to connector tabs/pins (photo 0 shows a cracked/taped area near the connector in photo 2)
risks.proof: Close-up of connector pins and housing integrity

proof_requests: Clear photo of the part number label on the second ECU (photo 2)
Video of the VW ECU (07K 906 055 CR) powering up or passing a bench/diagnostic test
Confirmation and proof that the ECU is unlocked/virgin (not immobilizer-paired to original car)
Close-up of the wiring connector end to assess damage/completeness
response.reason: The primary item is clearly identified by a legible VW/Bosch part number, so it can be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly immobilizer-locked, pulled ECU; the second unit in photo 2 is unidentified and excluded from pricing pending a label shot.
